entries.description: Row label in the algorithm input parameters list for an array value. %1$d is the number of elements; the actual value follows after the line break.
Title of the group of Auto ISF preferences.
Reason shown when autosens (automatic sensitivity detection) is off in preferences.
Button showing the input profile that Autotune will use. Short imperative.
Button opening a comparison of original and tuned profile. Short imperative.
Question in the confirmation dialog; the proposed new profile name follows on the next line.
Button (and confirmation dialog title) to copy the tuned profile into a new local profile. Short imperative.
Label for the number of days of past data Autotune analyses.
Description of the Autotune plugin: helps suggest adjustments of profile values (ISF, carb ratio, basal rates).
Error shown after a failed run: input data is faulty; try again or reduce the number of days.
Error shown after a failed run: input data insufficient; increase the number of days.
Warning that the profile has several IC (insulin to carb ratio) values but Autotune uses a single one. %1$d is count, %2$.2f the ratio in grams per unit.
Warning that the profile has several ISF (insulin sensitivity factor) values but Autotune uses a single one. %1$d count, %2$.1f value, %3$s glucose unit (mg/dL or mmol/L).
Label before the date of the last Autotune run. Ends with a colon.
Narrow column header: how much data was missing for this time slot or parameter.
Column header for the profile parameter name (ISF, IC, ...) in the results table. Very narrow column.
Progress message while running. %1$d is the current day tuned, %2$d the total number of days.
Row label in the Autotune results: insulin peak time of the active insulin curve. Short.
Narrow column header for the percent difference between original and tuned value. Just the percent sign in English.
Label of the dropdown that selects which profile to tune. Ends with a colon in English.
Warning that the selected profile is not valid, so Autotune cannot use it. Short.
Heading line of the result. %1$s is the date and time of the run.
Button (and confirmation dialog title) to restore the input profile from the one Autotune started with. Short imperative.
Question in the confirmation dialog. %1$s is the profile name.
Button starting an Autotune calculation; also the name of the Automation action. Short imperative.
Name given to the profile produced by Autotune (also used as file name). One word.
Button (and confirmation dialog title) to overwrite the input profile with the tuned values. Short imperative.
Question in the confirmation dialog. %1$s is the profile name.
Label before warnings about the selected profile. Ends with a colon.
Warning shown after a successful run: the user must review results before applying them to a profile.
Warning shown while the calculation is running, which takes a while.
Result text when the temporary basal request was already in place or applied correctly. Short.
Title of the notification that tells the user to eat carbohydrates because the algorithm predicts low glucose.
Section heading for the constraints (safety limits) applied to the algorithm result. Plural noun.
Description of the AMA plugin in the plugin list: it is an old algorithm, state of the art in 2017.
Description of the Auto ISF plugin in the plugin list: experimental, for advanced users.
Description of the Loop plugin in the plugin list: enables or disables the algorithm that triggers loop runs.
Description of the SMB plugin in the plugin list: recommended for advanced users.
No usage found in code.
Title of the percentage factor that scales the dynamic insulin sensitivity factor (ISF, how much one unit of insulin lowers glucose). Contains % as unit hint.
No usage found in code.
Reason shown when dynamic ISF cannot be used and the plain SMB algorithm is used because there is too little total daily dose (TDD) data.
Reason shown when the profile's fixed sensitivity (ISF) is used because dynamic data is missing. %1$s is the reason, already translated or English.
Fragment naming the cause of a limit: the fixed safety hard limit built into the app. Inserted into other messages, lowercase.
Action button on the carbs-required notification: ignore it for 15 minutes. Short button; m means minutes.
Action button on the carbs-required notification: ignore it for 30 minutes. Short button; m means minutes.
Action button on the carbs-required notification: ignore it for 5 minutes. Short button, limited space; m means minutes.

entries.ui_location: Constraint reason in loop result / Loop screen
entries.description: Reason text recorded when the max basal setting is raised because it is lower than the maximum basal in the profile. Basal is background insulin rate.
Label before the time of the last loop run. Short.
Reason that max insulin on board (IOB) is limited. %1$.1f is the limit in units (U), %2$s the cause, a fragment such as 'hard limit' or 'max value in preferences'.
Label before the name of the APS algorithm plugin used. APS is the abbreviation of artificial pancreas system; keep short.
Label before the algorithm result after safety constraints were applied.
Label before the time the SMB was sent to the pump.
Label before the time an SMB (super micro bolus, small automatic bolus) was requested.
Label before the SMB the pump confirmed it delivered.
Label before the time the temporary basal rate was sent to the pump.
Label before the time a temporary basal rate (TBR) was requested.
Label before the temporary basal the pump confirmed it is running.
Fragment inserted as the limiting cause into the 'limiting basal rate' reason: the profile max basal multiplier. Lowercase, not a sentence.
Fragment inserted as the limiting cause into the 'limiting basal rate' reason: the max daily basal multiplier. Lowercase fragment.
Fragment naming the cause of a limit: the value set in preferences. Inserted into other messages, lowercase.
Shown in the loop result when no algorithm plugin is selected or it gave no result. Uppercase on purpose.
Title of the notification (and message on the watch) shown in open loop mode when the algorithm has a new proposal the user has to accept.
Error shown when the user accepts an old open loop suggestion; nothing was sent to the pump.
Name of the Auto ISF algorithm plugin, an OpenAPS variant. Shown in the plugin list and as preference screen title.
Message shown in the algorithm result area when autosens (automatic sensitivity detection) has no data yet.
No usage found in code.
Name of the OpenAPS AMA algorithm plugin (AMA = advanced meal assist). Shown in the plugin list and as preference screen title.
Warning text on a clickable preference that opens documentation; tells advanced settings below normally should not be changed. Keeps capitalised CLICK HERE and READ for emphasis.
Section heading for autosens data (automatically detected sensitivity ratio).
Section heading showing the currently running temporary basal rate that is fed into the algorithm.
Message shown in the algorithm result area (and debug log) when the algorithm plugin is disabled.
Section heading showing the glucose status input (current value and deltas).
Group heading above the data given to the algorithm as input.
Section heading for insulin-on-board (IOB, active insulin) input data.
Label before the time of the last algorithm run. Short.
Section heading for meal data (carbs on board and absorption) input.
Message shown in the algorithm result area when there is no glucose reading to calculate from.
Section heading for the profile (basal, ISF, carb ratio, targets) input.
Section heading for the algorithm's result: the request for temp basal or SMB.
Section heading for the debug output of the algorithm script; technical.
Name of the OpenAPS SMB algorithm plugin (SMB = super micro bolus). Product name, shown in the plugin list and as the preference screen title.
Reason shown when a pump command is blocked or the running mode is 'disconnected': the pump was disconnected by the user. Short status phrase.
Message shown as loop result when the pump driver is not yet ready. Whole sentence.
Label before the algorithm's request (temp basal or SMB proposal), shown as full-width row.
Title of the group of preferences about how SMB (small automatic boluses) are delivered.
Reason shown when SMB (super micro bolus) is not allowed because the user turned it off in preferences.
Message when an SMB (super micro bolus) is skipped because a bolus was delivered in the last three minutes. Whole sentence.
Reason shown when UAM (unannounced meals detection) is off in preferences.
Alarm text when the pump rejected a zero temporary basal, so insulin might still be delivered; user is asked to check the pump. Important safety warning.
